terms.meaning: A systematic study of the past, built on when, where and who.
A moral story, the way Jesus taught.
Islam means peace or submission; a Muslim is one who surrenders to God.
The Prophet's move from Mecca to Madina, which starts the Islamic era.

items.name: Life of Jesus
items.formula: Born in Bethlehem (Israel) to Mary; at about 30 he left home to serve the poor.
items.example: Religious leaders accused him of treason and he was crucified.

items.name: Teachings of Jesus
items.formula: We are all God's children, so all brothers. "Love your neighbour as yourself."
items.example: Service to mankind is service to God.

items.name: Spread of Christianity
items.formula: His twelve disciples spread the teachings; Rome later recognised the faith.
items.example: Rome became the centre of the Church, with the Pope as its head.

items.name: Life of Prophet Muhammad
items.formula: Born at Mecca to Abdullah and Aminah; married Khadijah.
items.example: At forty he received prophethood in the cave of Hira; his messages form the Quran, in Arabic.

items.name: Teachings of Islam
items.formula: One God; traders must not cheat; no interest on loans.
items.example: Infanticide, alcohol and gambling are great sins.

items.name: Five religious practices of Islam
items.formula: Kalima (faith), Namaz (prayer five times a day), Roza (fasting in Ramzan), Zakath (giving to the poor), Haj (pilgrimage to Mecca).
items.example: Haj is done once in a lifetime.

items.name: Contributions of the Arabs
items.formula: Algebra, chemistry, astronomy; Unani medicine; they passed Indian numbers, including zero, to the West.
items.example: Baghdad was their centre of learning.

items.name: Famous works in Persian
items.formula: The Arabian Nights, Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat and Firdausi's Shahnamah.

items.name: The Crusades
items.formula: Nine wars between Christians and Muslims for Palestine and Jerusalem.
items.example: Main cause: the Turks stopped Christian pilgrims entering Palestine.

items.name: Outcome of the Crusades
items.formula: About 40,000 took Jerusalem in the first; later ones, like the fourth with about 50,000, failed.
items.example: Christians lost the holy land, but Europe-Asia trade grew.

items.name: Genghis Khan and Qublai Khan
items.formula: Genghis Khan united the Mongols; his grandson Qublai Khan became Emperor of China.
items.example: Qublai fed the hungry in famines and became a Buddhist.

items.name: Timur
items.formula: Conquered Persia, Iraq, Syria and Afghanistan, and invaded India.
items.example: Babur, founder of Mughal rule, was from his line.

items.name: Ottoman Turks
items.formula: Nomads from Turkistan (now Turkmenistan) who became Muslims and built the Ottoman military state.
items.example: Turks set up the Delhi Sultanate in India.

mistakes.text: Qublai Khan was Genghis Khan's grandson, not his son.
The Rubaiyat and Shahnamah are in Persian, though they are counted among the Arabs' contributions.
Jesus was born in Bethlehem; Prophet Muhammad was born in Mecca.
